question:
Does any golden-visa class exist in the corpus, with which investment tiers and stay durations?

Use only the sources already in NB-2. Answer with concrete conclusions, do not default to requesting human review. Separate primary regulatory sources, official operational sources, and internal interpretations. For every claim give source title, date, passage and source ID. Distinguish what is legally permitted, what is operationally available, and what requires document verification. List the decisive facts, missing questions, alternatives and conflicts. If the sources do not allow a conclusion, state exactly which information or source is missing.
answer:
Yes, a dedicated **Golden Visa** program officially exists in the Indonesian legal framework under the current corpus. Defined under national law (*Permenkumham No. 22 Tahun 2023*, Bab V, Pasal 184), the Golden Visa represents a specific grouping of Limited Stay Visas (VITAS), Limited Stay Permits (ITAS/KITAS), Permanent Stay Permits (ITAP/KITAP), and Re-entry Permits (MERP) granted for extended durations to select foreigners [1].

Here is a highly precise normative and operational breakdown of the Golden Visa classes, investment tiers, and stay durations, separated strictly by the nature of the sources as requested [2, 3].

---

### I. PROFILO NORMATIVO: PRIMARY REGULATORY SOURCES (NATIONAL LEGISLATION)
These represent the binding statutory rules, government regulations, and ministerial decrees enacted by the central government of the Republic of Indonesia.

#### 1. Legally Permitted Activities & Stay Durations
Under **Pasal 185 Ayat (1) of Permenkumham No. 22/2023**, Golden Visas are legally permitted for four macro-categories: Penanaman Modal (Investment), Penyatuan Keluarga (Family Reunification), Repatriasi (Repatriation), and Rumah Kedua (Second Home) [4]. Under **Pasal 185 Ayat (2)**, these permits are granted for a maximum stay duration of **5 years** or **10 years** [4].

#### 2. Investment Tiers (Authoritative National Thresholds)
Under **Permenkumham No. 11 Tahun 2024** (amending Permenkumham No. 22/2023), the investment tiers are strictly codified as follows [5, 6]:

*   **Corporate Investors (Establishing a New PT PMA) — Index E28B** [3]:
    *   **5-Year Duration**: Requires a minimum capital commitment (modal ditempatkan/saham) or investment value of **USD 2,500,000** (*Pasal 39 Ayat 2*) [7, 8].
    *   **10-Year Duration**: Requires a minimum capital commitment or investment value of **USD 5,000,000** (*Pasal 40 Ayat 2*) [9, 10].
*   **Existing PMA Shareholder Variant — Index E28A/E28B**:
    *   Stranieri who already hold shares in an existing PMA company can qualify by documenting share ownership of at least **Rp 10,000,000,000** (ten billion Rupiah) (*Pasal 38 Ayat 2 Huruf a*) [11].
*   **Pure Portfolio Investors (No Company) — Index E28C** [12]:
    *   **5-Year Duration**: Requires a commitment to purchase Indonesian government bonds (SBN), shares in public companies, or mutual funds in public companies of at least **USD 350,000** (*Pasal 39 Ayat 3*) [8, 13, 14].
    *   **10-Year Duration**: Requires a commitment to purchase Indonesian government bonds (SBN), public company shares, or public mutual funds of at least **USD 700,000** (*Pasal 40 Ayat 3 Huruf a-c*) [10, 15, 16]. Alternatively, a commitment to buy a residential condominium/apartment in Indonesia worth at least **USD 1,000,000** (*Pasal 40 Ayat 3 Huruf d*) [16, 17].
*   **Second Home / Silver Visa — Index E33A & E33B** [18]:
    *   **E33A (Property)**: Requires the purchase of a residential property/condominium of at least **Rp 2,000,000,000** nationally [19, 20].
    *   **E33B (Deposit)**: Requires a minimum bank balance of **USD 130,000** (or equivalent Rp 2,000,000,000) deposited in an Indonesian state-owned bank (Bank BUMN) under the applicant's name (*Pasal 56 Ayat 2*) [21, 22].

#### 3. Strict Document Verification Requirements (*Jaminan Keimigrasian*)
Golden Visa holders are exempt from the standard requirement of having a local sponsor (penjamin) under *Pasal 4 and 6 of Permenkumham 11/2024* [23, 24]. Instead, they operate under the **Jaminan Keimigrasian** (Immigration Guarantee) framework, which requires rigorous document verification [25]:
*   **Initial Verification**: Passport validity must cover the stay duration [26]. The applicant must submit a formal statement of commitment (*Pernyataan Komitmen*) [27], proof of sufficient life expenses for themselves and their family [11], and bank statements [28].
*   **Fulfillment Period (90 Days)**: Under **Pasal 40 Ayat (3) of Permenkumham 11/2024**, proof of actual financial fulfillment (e.g., share certificate, bank deposit, bond statement) must be submitted to the local Immigration Office within **90 days** of ITAS concession [29]. **Failure to comply results in immediate permit revocation [30, 31].**
*   **Annual Audit**: Under **Pasal 198 of Permenkumham 22/2023**, the Directorate General of Immigration or designated local officers conduct an annual evaluation of the *Jaminan Keimigrasian* to ensure the investment remains active [32, 33].

> *   **Primary Regulatory Citation 1**: *Peraturan Menteri Hukum dan HAM Nomor 22 Tahun 2023* | Date: 2023-08-22 | Passage Index: 83, 84, 85, 86 | Source ID: JDIH Kemenkumham [1, 4, 32, 34]
> *   **Primary Regulatory Citation 2**: *Peraturan Menteri Hukum dan HAM Nomor 11 Tahun 2024* | Date: 2024-04-01 | Passage Index: 145, 146, 148, 149 | Source ID: peraturan.bpk.go.id [8, 10, 14, 16]

---

### II. PRASSI SUL CAMPO: OFFICIAL OPERATIONAL SOURCES
These encompass the operational mechanisms of the newly formed **Kemenimipas** (Ministry of Immigration and Correctional Affairs, established in late 2024 [35, 36]), its electronic platforms, and regional enforcement channels.

#### 1. Operationally Available Application Pathways
*   **Digital Portals**: Domestically, the system is processed online through the e-Visa / Molina portals [37, 38]. 
*   **Automatic MERP**: Under the *Omnibus Law reform of UU No. 63/2024*, the Multiple Exit Re-entry Permit (MERP) is operationally integrated automatically into the KITAS/KITAP upon issuance [39, 40]. No separate applications or separate fees are required to exit/enter the country [39, 40].
*   **The "Riwayat Tinggal" (Previous Stay History) Prerequisite**: To operationally unlock a **10-year Golden Visa**, the applicant must show a documented history of previous stays (*riwayat tinggal*) in Indonesia (specifically, having entered using a 5-year multiple-entry visa in the past 3 years) under *Pasal 16 Ayat (2) of Permenkumham 11/2024* [41, 42].

#### 2. Bali-Specific Local Deviations
*   **E33A Property Minimum**: Nationally, the property threshold is Rp 2 billion [19]. However, under local Balinese rules (**Perda Bali No. 2/2025**, formerly *Perda No. 6/2023*), the regional minimum is elevated to **Rp 5,000,000,000** (five billion Rupiah) and is strictly limited to strata title (Hak Pakai) [19, 43].
*   **Bali Tourist Levy**: Every visitor entering Bali must pay the local **Rp 150,000 Bali Tourist Levy** via the "Love Bali" portal [44]. KITAS/KITAP holders are technically exempt but must submit an exemption request on lovebali.baliprov.go.id [44, 45].
*   **Patrols & Local Surveillance**: Bali's **Dharma Dewata Patrol Task Force** (launched in April 2026) actively monitors social media and co-working/hotspot areas (Canggu, Ubud) [46]. They aggressively enforce the prohibition on tourist visas or non-work visas conducting unpaid local business promotions or bartering in-kind value exchanges (such as free villa stays in exchange for influencer content) [46, 47].

> *   **Official Operational Citation 1**: *Kepmen M.IP-08.GR.01.01/2025 — Klasifikasi Visa* | Date: 2025-05-02 | Passage Index: 1-14 | Source ID: Kemenimipas [48-51]
> *   **Official Operational Citation 2**: *Bali Tourist Levy — Perda Bali 2/2025 (was 6/2023)* | Date: 2026-03-28 | Passage Index: 434, 435, 436 | Source ID: Regional Government of Bali [44, 45, 52]

---

### III. VALUTAZIONE TECNICA: INTERNAL INTERPRETATIONS & EXPERT GUIDES
These analyses are compiled from client dossiers, cross-validation registers, and operational guides maintained by immigration specialists (*Zantara / Bali Zero Intelligence*) [2, 37].

#### 1. Estimated Agency Timelines and Costs
According to internal databases, processing fees (inclusive of government PNBP fees) and timelines for Golden Visas processed through local agencies are structured as [53]:
*   **KITAS E28B (Golden Visa 5Y)**: **Rp 45,000,000 – Rp 65,000,000** | Timeline: **8–16 weeks** (includes PT PMA setup support) [53].
*   **KITAS E28G (Golden Visa 10Y)**: **Rp 55,000,000 – Rp 75,000,000** | Timeline: **10–18 weeks** [53].

#### 2. Strategic Selection Criteria (*E28B vs. E28C*)
*   **E28B** is interpreted as the ideal vehicle for active entrepreneurs who intend to establish and operate a company (PT PMA) and legally hold a position as a Director (*Direktur*) or Commissioner (*Komisaris*) [54].
*   **E28C** is reserved for pure portfolio HNWI (High Net Worth Individuals) who seek residence and capital appreciation but wish to avoid corporate management obligations [55, 56]. They are legally barred from active work or sales of goods/services [57].

> *   **Internal Expert Citation 1**: *kitas_e28b_e28c_golden_visa_guida_2025.txt* | Date: 2025-03-27 | Passage Index: 230-251 | Source ID: Bali Zero Intelligence [2, 54, 57]
> *   **Internal Expert Citation 2**: *nb2_golden_visa.txt* | Date: 2026-03-28 | Passage Index: 279-287 | Source ID: Bali Zero Knowledge Base [18, 19, 58-61]

---

### IV. CONCRETE DECISIONS, CONFLICTS, AND GAPS
This section provides an expert legal assessment of the critical discrepancies, discrepancies, and legislative omissions in the current framework.

#### 1. The Authoritative Investment Tier Conflict (The E28B 10-Year Correction)
*   **The Conflict**: The initial master guide for Golden Visas (*kitas_e28b_e28c_golden_visa_guida_2025.txt*) erroneously recorded that the minimum corporate investment for *both* the 5-year and 10-year E28B variants was USD 2,500,000 [62].
*   **The Decisive Correction**: Cross-validation with *Permenkumham 11/2024 Pasal 39 Ayat (2) and Pasal 40 Ayat (2)* confirmed that while the **5-year E28B requires USD 2,500,000**, the **10-year E28B strictly requires USD 5,000,000** [63]. This was formally corrected in the *ERRATA CORRIGE of March 28, 2026* [62]. Clients must prepare USD 5M for the 10-year visa, as under-funding will cause application rejection [64].

#### 2. The E28G Index / Investment Tier Discrepancy
*   **The Mismatch**: Internal databases (*nb2_visa_types_final.txt*, Index E28G) define **E28G** as "Golden Visa 10Y" with an investment threshold of **Rp 5 miliar+** or **USD 700,000** [43, 65]. This represents a serious structural misalignment:
    1.  Nationally, under *Permenkumham 11/2024*, the corporate 10-year investment is **USD 5,000,000** (E28B) [63], and the portfolio 10-year investment is **USD 700,000** (E28C) [64].
    2.  A threshold of "Rp 5 billion" (approx. USD 310,000) for a 10-year Golden Visa (E28G) is a clear mismatch and does not align with the USD 5,000,000 corporate threshold required by national law. 
*   **Alternative / Resolution**: Clients must follow the national law (*Permenkumham 11/2024*) and prepare **USD 5,000,000** for corporate establishment or **USD 700,000** for portfolio investments [63, 64].

#### 3. Unresolved Gaps & Missing Information (Open Questions Register)
*   **OQ-002: Automatic MERP Integration Scope**: While *UU No. 63/2024* eliminates the MERP as a separate booklet, the specific *Petunjuk Teknis (Juknis)* from the newly formed Kemenimipas detailing whether automatic MERP functions without any manual backend activation for E28/E33 series is still unverified [66].
*   **OQ-003: Overriding Legislation (UU No. 1 Tahun 2026)**: Rumors of an overriding immigration law, "UU Nomor 1 Tahun 2026," are recorded in the pipeline, but the text is missing from the JDIH primary database in this session, representing a critical temporal gap in validating whether the 2024 reforms have been amended [67].

> *   **Conflict/Correction Citation**: *ERRATA CORRIGE — Golden Visa E28B Investment Thresholds* | Date: 2026-03-28 | Passage Index: 437, 438, 439 | Source ID: NB2-Q17-001 [62-64]
> *   **Gaps Citation**: *[NB2-MD] Open Questions - Updated 2026-03-28* | Date: 2026-03-28 | Passage Index: 93, 94, 95 | Source ID: MD-2 [66-68]

b) Investitori stranieri (E28A, E33G) Non è richiesto un garante per investitori stranieri che investono in Indonesia [IMM-249, IMM-349]. Gli investitori operano senza un garante tradizionale, ma in sostituzione versano una garanzia finanziaria (jaminan keimigrasian) [IMM-251]. Il Visa E28A (investor) richiede un investimento minimo di 10 miliardi di rupiah o il possesso di obbligazioni statali [IMM-004]. Gli investitori stranieri devono impegnare investimenti di almeno 2,5 milioni di dollari entro 90 giorni dalla concessione del permesso di soggiorno limitato [IMM-311].

Stranieri investitori di capitale estero possono soggiornare per periodi di massimo 2 anni (tipologia base E28A) [IMM-290], massimo 5 anni [IMM-291], oppure massimo 10 anni [IMM-292] a seconda della categoria e del livello di impegno documentato. Il passaporto dello straniero deve essere valido per tutta la durata del soggiorno richiesto [IMM-027]. ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ 2. ============================================================ SEZIONE C: INVESTOR E GOLDEN VISA Q: Voglio investire in Indonesia. Quale visa è meglio? R: Dipende dall'importo e dal tipo. Per piccolo investimento in PT PMA: KITAS E28A (Investor standard). Per importi maggiori: Golden Visa E28B (5 anni, USD 350K) o E28G (10 anni, USD 700K). Per properti: E33A. Q: Con il Golden Visa posso lavorare? R: Dipende. Con E28B come direktur di PT PMA propria: sì. Con E33B (deposito): no, solo residenza. Q: Quanto costa comprare properti a Bali per il Second Home Visa? R: Min Rp2 miliar nazionale, ma a Bali la Perda locale richiede min Rp5 miliar per strata title. Solo strata title è accessibile agli stranieri (Hak Pakai, non Hak Milik).

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Section 4 — PLAIN-LANGUAGE DEFINITION (5 bullets, citable) What the C5A "Visa Kunjungan Konten Kreator" BANS and PERMITS — for an Indonesian content-creator beneficiary: PERMITTED — creating content. A C5A holder may shoot, film and produce social-media content in Indonesia. That creative act is the visa's purpose ("Visa Kunjungan Konten Kreator"). (Basis: the visa category itself, Kepmen M.IP-08.GR.01.01/2025; sibling C5 "Dengan visa ini, anda dapat ... peliputan".) PERMITTED — being paid by a FOREIGN source. Income from outside Indonesia — a foreign brand, a foreign agency, Google AdSense (Google Ireland/US), a foreign employer — does not trigger the prohibition, because the ban is specifically on reward "dari perorangan atau korporasi DI INDONESIA." (The E33G row confirms the same logic: it requires "perjanjian kerja dengan perusahaan yang didirikan di luar Wilayah Indonesia.") BANNED — selling goods or services locally. Selling any product or service while on this visa is prohibited: "dilarang menjual barang atau jasa." (Basis: C5 , live; same family for C5A.) BANNED — any reward from an Indonesian person or company, INCLUDING in-kind/barter. Receiving "imbalan, upah, atau sejenisnya ... dari perorangan atau korporasi di Indonesia" is prohibited. "Imbalan ... atau sejenisnya" (reward ... or the like) covers non-monetary compensation — a free villa/hotel stay, a sponsored experience, services in kind — because Indonesian labour law itself counts "imbalan dalam bentuk lain" (reward in another form) as compensation (UU 13/2003 Pasal 1 angka 3-4). No money has to change hands for it to be banned. WHY — it's the SOURCE and the BENEFICIARY, not the cash. Indonesian immigration judges the substance of the activity: purpose of arrival, form of activity, and economic impact — and criminalises activity inconsistent with the permit (UU 6/2011 Pasal 122), with the enabling Indonesian party exposed to the same penalty (Pasal 122 letter b). Work that benefits an Indonesian business and is rewarded by that Indonesian business is, in substance, local employment requiring a work permit/RPTKA (PP 34/2021) — barter does not escape this.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ 3.1 Chi può richiederlo (no azienda) ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ Il KITAS E28C è riservato agli investitori individuali stranieri che NON intendono costituire o partecipare a una PT PMA, ma desiderano soggiornare in Indonesia grazie a un impegno di investimento diretto in strumenti finanziari dello Stato o di banche statali indonesiane [IMM-313], [IMM-381]. Il profilo tipico è quello dell'investitore patrimoniale, del gestore di patrimonio privato o dell'HNWI (High Net Worth Individual) che vuole risiedere in Indonesia senza gestire un'azienda operativa.

Molti investitori che già possiedono o vogliono aprire una PT PMA a Bali scelgono E28B. L'E28C è adatto a chi cerca pura residenza fiscale e patrimoniale senza impegni operativi aziendali. 6.2 Tempistica impegni Entrambe le categorie impongono un impegno entro 90 giorni dall'ingresso [IMM-311], [IMM-316], [IMM-382]. Questo significa che il cliente deve essere pronto a completare l'investimento (aprire il deposito, acquistare SBN, versare capitale societario) entro circa 3 mesi dall'arrivo. Bali Zero assiste in tutto il processo documentale.

question:
Does the corpus address tax-residency interaction (183-day rule) for long-stay visitors/remote workers, or is that outside immigration scope? Distinguish the immigration fact (source/activity of income) from the tax-residency question — where must the engine only warn, not decide.

Use only the sources already in NB-2. Answer with concrete conclusions, do not default to requesting human review. Separate primary regulatory sources, official operational sources, and internal interpretations. For every claim give source title, date, passage and source ID. Distinguish what is legally permitted, what is operationally available, and what requires document verification. List the decisive facts, missing questions, alternatives and conflicts. If the sources do not allow a conclusion, state exactly which information or source is missing.
answer:
### Executive Summary

The interaction between **tax residency** (the **183-day rule**) and **immigration status** is a critical compliance domain for long-stay visitors and remote workers in Indonesia. The corpus explicitly addresses this interaction, confirming that while tax-residency status is technically governed by fiscal regulations outside the core administrative scope of the Ministry of Immigration and Correctional Services (Kemenimipas) [1, 2], it heavily intersects with immigration compliance [3, 4].

To avoid systemic regulatory errors, any compliance engine must strictly distinguish between **immigration facts** (which the engine can **decide**) and **tax-residency questions** (where the engine must **only warn**):

1. **Immigration Facts (Source and Activity of Income):** These are binary, statutory determinations regarding whether a foreigner's activities are legally permitted under their specific visa category [5, 6]. The engine can **decide** eligibility here because immigration authorities have sole jurisdiction over whether the source of work and beneficiary of the activity are local or foreign [5, 7].
2. **Tax-Residency Questions (Duration of Stay & Fiscal Liability):** These are subjective, quantitative determinations governed by the Directorate General of Taxes (DJP) based on physical presence (staying **more than 183 days** in any 12-month period) [3, 4]. Because a foreigner can remain completely in compliance with immigration rules while simultaneously triggering tax residency (e.g., on a 1-year E33G KITAS) [3, 8], the engine **must only warn, not decide**, on tax liabilities [3]. Tax residency involves subjective intent, bilateral double taxation treaties (P3B) [3], and global income declarations that fall outside the jurisdiction of immigration law.

---

### Regulatory Hierarchy of Sources

Every legal claim regarding the 183-day rule, remote work parameters, and tax interaction is categorized below under the appropriate tier of the Indonesian legal hierarchy.

#### 1. Primary Regulatory Sources (National Legislation & Decrees)
These national-level statutes and government regulations establish the absolute legal boundaries for stay permits, employment, and fiscal liabilities.

*   **Claim 1:** Remote workers (Digital Nomads) must perform their work exclusively for entities registered outside Indonesian territory, and their stay permit (E33G) is limited to a maximum of 1 year.
    *   **Source Title:** *Permenkumham No. 22 Tahun 2023 tentang Visa dan Izin Tinggal* (as amended by *Permenkumham No. 11/2024*).
    *   **Date:** August 22, 2023 / 2024.
    *   **Passage:** "pekerja jarak jauh (remote worker) yang terikat hubungan kerja dengan perusahaan di luar Wilayah Indonesia untuk jangka waktu paling lama 1 (satu) tahun." [9-11]
    *   **Source ID:** Passage [9], Claim ID: [IMM-363] / [IMM-364].
*   **Claim 2:** All foreign nationals are criminally liable if they perform activities within Indonesian territory that do not align with the specific purpose of their stay permit.
    *   **Source Title:** *Undang-Undang No. 6 Tahun 2011 tentang Keimigrasian* (as amended by *UU No. 63/2024*).
    *   **Date:** 2011 / 2024.
    *   **Passage:** "Dipidana dengan pidana penjara paling lama 5 (lima) tahun... setiap Orang Asing yang dengan sengaja menyalahgunakan atau melakukan kegiatan yang tidak sesuai dengan maksud dan tujuan Izin Tinggal yang diberikan kepadanya." [12]
    *   **Source ID:** Passage [12], Article 122 letter a.
*   **Claim 3:** Legal "work" under Indonesian law is defined by the substance and intent of the activity, and employers are defined as those who pay wages or any other form of "in-kind" reward.
    *   **Source Title:** *Undang-Undang No. 13 Tahun 2003 tentang Ketenagakerjaan* / *PP No. 34 Tahun 2021 tentang Penggunaan Tenaga Kerja Asing*.
    *   **Date:** 2003 / 2021.
    *   **Passage:** "Pemberi kerja adalah... yang mempekerjakan tenaga kerja dengan membayar upah atau imbalan dalam bentuk lain." [13, 14] and "Tenaga Kerja Asing... adalah warga negara asing pemegang visa dengan maksud bekerja di wilayah Indonesia." [15]
    *   **Source ID:** Passage [13], Pasal 1 angka 4; Passage [15], Pasal 1 angka 1.
*   **Claim 4:** Multiple Exit Re-entry Permits (MERP) are automatically integrated into all KITAS types (including E33G remote work and E28A investment) upon issuance under the new Omnibus framework.
    *   **Source Title:** *UU No. 63 Tahun 2024 — Perubahan atas UU Keimigrasian (Key Provisions)*.
    *   **Date:** 2024.
    *   **Passage:** "UU 63/2024 menghapus kebutuhan MERP... Izin masuk kembali (re-entry permit) otomatis terintegrasi dalam KITAS dan KITAP sejak tanggal penerbitan... Berlaku untuk: Semua jenis KITAS (E23 pekerja, E28 investor... E33g remote work)." [16]
    *   **Source ID:** Passage [16], Section 1.

#### 2. Official Operational Sources
These represent the operational directives, portal rules, and official enforcement communications from the Directorate General of Immigration (Ditjen Imigrasi).

*   **Claim 5:** To obtain the E33G Remote Work visa, the applicant must operationally upload a remote employment contract with a company registered outside Indonesia and prove an annual income of at least USD 60,000.
    *   **Source Title:** *2026-06-01-c5a-local-ban-sources.md* (verbatim extraction of public portal specifications).
    *   **Date:** June 1, 2026.
    *   **Passage:** "Perjanjian kerja dengan perusahaan yang didirikan di luar Wilayah Indonesia" — and proof of "penghasilan... senilai paling sedikit US\$60.000 per tahun." [17]
    *   **Source ID:** Passage [17], Section 1b.
*   **Claim 6:** Any activity resembling work that provides economic benefit to a local business, even if unpaid or conducted under a non-monetary barter agreement, is strictly illegal on visitor or tourist visas.
    *   **Source Title:** *Ditjen Imigrasi Official Instagram Statements* (as reported by local registries).
    *   **Date:** May 23, 2026.
    *   **Passage:** "Aktivitas yang menyerupai pekerjaan dan memberikan manfaat ekonomi, meskipun tidak dibayar... Yang dinilai bukan hanya apakah seseorang dibayar atau tidak, tetapi juga tujuan kedatangan, bentuk kegiatan, dan dampak ekonominya." [18]
    *   **Source ID:** Passage [18], Section 3c.

#### 3. Internal Interpretations (Expert Legal Guides)
These are expert operational interpretations compiled by Bali Zero / Zantara Intelligence based on real client case files, local office practices, and tax-immigration crossovers.

*   **Claim 7:** Staying in Indonesia for more than 183 days in a single tax year triggers subjective and objective tax residency, exposing the remote worker's global income to Indonesian tax laws.
    *   **Source Title:** *kitas_e33g_remote_work_guida_2025.txt* / *nb2_faq_clienti.txt*.
    *   **Date:** March 27, 2025 / March 2026.
    *   **Passage:** "il titolare di E33G che risiede in Indonesia per più di 183 giorni/anno fiscale diventa RESIDENTE FISCALE indonesiano. Conseguenze: Obbligo di registrazione NPWP personale... I redditi esteri POSSONO essere soggetti a tassazione indonesiana (applicazione del principio di residenza fiscale globale dal 2025)." [3]
    *   **Source ID:** Passage [3], Section 8; Passage [19].
*   **Claim 8:** E28A Investor KITAS holders are subject to identical fiscal obligations if their physical stay exceeds the 183-day limit.
    *   **Source Title:** *visto_e28a_investitore_guida_2025.txt*.
    *   **Date:** March 27, 2025.
    *   **Passage:** "L'investitore straniero titolare di KITAS E28A è considerato residente fiscale in Indonesia se soggiorna per più di 183 giorni in un periodo di 12 mesi... Principali obblighi: Registrazione... e ottenimento del... (NPWP) entro 1 mese dall'arrivo." [4]
    *   **Source ID:** Passage [4], Section 6.

---

### Permitted vs. Operationally Available vs. Document Verification

To structure a compliance system, activities and requirements must be categorized into three distinct execution states:

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                                  COMPLIANCE MATRIX                                      │
├──────────────────────────┬───────────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────────┤
│    LEGALLY PERMITTED     │  OPERATIONALLY AVAILABLE  │      DOCUMENT VERIFICATION       │
│     (Statutory Right)    │     (System Function)     │       (Gatekeeping Proof)        │
├──────────────────────────┼───────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────┤
│ - Work for foreign-only  │ - Online e-Visa application│ - Original passport valid for    │
│   employers (E33G) [20] │   via Molina portal [21] │   at least 18 months (E33G) [22]│
│ - Opening local bank     │ - Automatic MERP          │ - Certified employment contract  │
│   accounts [23]         │   integration [16]       │   with a foreign company [17]    │
│ - Leasing local resid.   │ - In-country change of    │ - Bank statements proving income │
│   property [23]         │   status (Alih Status)    │   of >= USD 60,000/yr [17]       │
│ - Passive investment &   │   from C1/C18 to E33G [24]│ - Proof of local address         │
│   shareholding (E28A)    │                           │   (rental/booking) [22]         │
└──────────────────────────┴───────────────────────────┴──────────────────────────────────┘
```

#### A. Legally Permitted (What the Law Authorizes)
*   **Remote Work for Foreign Entities:** Under **PP 40/2023**, a foreigner holding an E33G visa is legally permitted to perform professional tasks within Indonesian territory, provided the employer is established outside Indonesia and the work does not target or interact with the local market [20].
*   **Local Financial Transactions:** Remote workers are legally permitted to lease private residential properties and open local bank accounts (e.g., BCA, Mandiri) to maintain their living expenses [23].
*   **Exclusion from Work Permits:** Under **PP 34/2021**, E33G and E28A holders are legally exempt from the requirement to obtain a local work permit (RPTKA) or pay the monthly USD 100 TKA compensation tax (DKP-TKA) [4, 25].

#### B. Operationally Available (What the Portals Execute)
*   **Molina Portal Applications:** Applications for E33G must be processed electronically through the Directorate General of Immigration's digital portal (`evisa.imigrasi.go.id` / Molina) [21, 26].
*   **In-Country Conversions (Alih Status):** Foreigners holding a valid **C1** (Tourist Visa) or **C18** (Work Trial) are operationally permitted to convert their status to an E33G KITAS without exiting the country, provided the application is made before the visa expires [24].
*   **Automated MERP:** Upon the electronic issuance of the E-ITAS, the immigration system automatically registers the holder for multiple entry and exit privileges [8, 27].

#### C. Requires Document Verification (What the Underwriter Must Validate)
*   **Income Verification:** The applicant must provide 3 to 6 months of bank statements proving a monthly salary of at least **USD 2,000** (or an annual tax return showing **USD 60,000** of foreign-sourced income) [22].
*   **Passport Validity Gate:** For immigration to issue the 1-year E33G KITAS, the applicant's passport must be verified to have a minimum validity of **18 months** [22]. 
*   **Foreign Corporate Status:** The sponsoring employer's corporate registration documents must be verified to ensure they have no local legal presence or branch office in Indonesia, preserving the "foreign-sourced" status of the income [20].

---

### Decisive Facts, Alternatives, and Conflicts

#### 1. Decisive Facts (The Compliance Hinge)
The **definitive fact** that legally validates an E33G Remote Worker visa over a standard E23 Working KITAS is **the geographical location and target market of the beneficiary** [5, 7]. If the foreigner provides professional services to an entity or individual *inside* Indonesia—or receives any reward (including comped stays or in-kind services) from an Indonesian source—the E33G is legally voided [7, 23]. The activity immediately defaults to local work, requiring a local corporate sponsor, an approved RPTKA, and an E23 visa [5, 28].

#### 2. Alternative Compliance Paths
*   **The Visit Visa Option (C1 / C2):** For remote workers staying less than 180 days per year, a C1 (Tourist) or C2 (Business) visa offers a valid alternative to avoid triggering tax residency [19, 29]. However, the C1/C2 does not permit any local work or local income and requires a "visa run" or strict exit planning once the 180-day stay limit is reached [30, 31].
*   **The PMA Investor Option (E28A):** If the remote worker wishes to establish a local business or invest in local real estate, they can establish a PT PMA (foreign-owned corporation) and transition to an E28A Investor KITAS, bypassing the strict foreign-source income rules of the E33G [32, 33].

#### 3. Legal and Operational Conflicts
*   **The 183-Day "Tax Trap":** The E33G visa is legally issued for a duration of 1 year [25]. However, staying for the full duration of the visa automatically triggers Indonesian **resident tax status** under the 183-day rule [3]. This exposes the nomad's *global* income to Indonesian tax authorities (DJP), creating a direct conflict with the "tax-free digital nomad" marketing narrative commonly found in public forums [19].
*   **Corporate Shareholder Renewal Bans:** A local conflict has emerged under the *Circular Imigrasi of March 31, 2026*, which prohibits foreign nationals who are registered shareholders or directors in local PT PMAs from renewing or holding standard C1 tourist visas [34]. They are forced to transition to E28A investor visas or face immediate rejection [34].

---

### Legal Gaps, Missing Information, and Uncertainties

Despite the detail provided in the expert guides, several critical legal gaps exist within the corpus, preventing a definitive, system-level determination on certain edge cases:

1.  **Absence of the Official C5A Decree text:** The official Directorate General of Immigration page for the **C5A (Content Creator Visa)** reads **"Data Belum Tersedia"** ("Data Not Yet Available") [35]. The precise regulatory restrictions (*Larangan*) for content creators are currently reconstructed from sibling indices (C5 media) and internal expert databases [35]. The official implementing regulation (*Petunjuk Teknis/Juknis*) is completely missing from the national archive [36, 37].
2.  **Supercession of Ministries:** There is an active administrative conflict between *Permenkumham No. 22/2023* (issued under the old Ministry of Law and Human Rights) and *Permenimipas No. 5/2025* (issued under the newly formed Ministry of Immigration and Correctional Services) [1, 38]. The exact extent to which the 2025 regulations supersede the 2023 provisions remains an **unresolved open question** in the operational change log (OQ-005) [38].
3.  **Ambiguity of "Intend to Reside Permanently":** Under national tax guidelines, tax residency can be triggered *before* Day 183 if the foreigner "intends to reside permanently" in Indonesia [4]. The exact objective metrics used by the tax office (DJP) to define "intent" (e.g., signing a 3-year villa lease or opening local accounts) are missing from the corpus, leaving a major compliance blind spot for the advisory engine.

"Pemberi kerja adalah orang perseorangan, pengusaha, badan hukum, atau badan-badan lainnya yang mempekerjakan tenaga kerja dengan membayar upah atau imbalan dalam bentuk lain ." EN: "An employer is a natural person, entrepreneur, legal entity, or other body that employs labour by paying a wage or reward in another form ." Analysis (this is the load-bearing nuance — handle precisely in the piece): The narrow term "upah" (angka 30) is, on its face, monetary ("dinyatakan dalam bentuk uang"). If the editorial relied ONLY on the labour-law definition of upah , a literalist could argue a free villa is "not upah" because no money moves. BUT the legal concepts that actually define WHO is a worker and WHO is an employer (angka 3 and angka 4) both explicitly include "imbalan dalam bentuk lain" — reward in another form , i.e. non-monetary / in-kind . Indonesian labour law itself therefore treats an in-kind reward as enough to constitute an employment relationship. This dovetails exactly with the immigration Larangan 's "imbalan, upah, atau sejenisnya" : the immigration text deliberately lists "imbalan" FIRST (the broad, not-necessarily-monetary term) and adds "atau sejenisnya" (or the like). It is not limited to "upah"/cash. A comped villa night given by an Indonesian villa in exchange for a Reel is an "imbalan ... dari ... korporasi di Indonesia" — squarely inside the ban.

Citable formulation for the piece: "Indonesian labour law defines a worker as anyone who works for a wage or reward in another form (UU 13/2003 Pasal 1 angka 3), and an employer as anyone who pays a wage or reward in another form (angka 4). The immigration prohibition mirrors this: it bans receiving imbalan, upah, atau sejenisnya — reward, wage, or the like . In-kind value (a free stay) is imbalan . No money needs to change hands." --------------------------------------------------------------------------------

In qualità di esperto di diritto dell'immigrazione indonesiano, viene presentata di seguito l'analisi normativa e operativa in merito all'**Izin Belajar** (permesso di studio) e ai visti ad esso collegati (**KITAS E30** e visti di visita **C9**), basata esclusivamente sul quadro giuridico e documentale di NB-2.

---

### 1. CONCLUSIONE GIURIDICA DI SINTESI E RILEVAZIONE DELLE LACUNE (GAP)

Dall'esame rigoroso delle fonti fornite, emerge una conclusione netta: **l'istituto specifico denominato "Izin Belajar" (permesso di studio ministeriale esterno) non è disciplinato né menzionato nei testi normativi sull'immigrazione presenti in NB-2 [1-4].** 

Di conseguenza:
1. **Autorità emittente**: Le fonti non indicano quale autorità esterna (come il Ministero dell'Educazione, della Cultura, della Ricerca e della Tecnologia - *Kemendikbudristek* o il Ministero degli Affari Religiosi - *Kemenag*) emetta l'Izin Belajar.
2. **Tipologie di istituti**: Le fonti non specificano quali categorie di istituti scolastici richiedano l'Izin Belajar, facendo riferimento solo genericamente a "istituti di istruzione registrati" (*institusi pendidikan terdaftar*) [5] o "corporazioni/istituti di istruzione" (*korporasi/lembaga pendidikan*) [1].
3. **Precondizione del visto di studio**: Ai sensi della legge sull'immigrazione primaria (*Permenkumham No. 22 del 2023*), l'Izin Belajar **non è menzionato come precondizione o requisito documentale formale** per il rilascio del visto di studio limitato (KITAS E30) [1, 2]. L'unico documento accademico richiesto come precondizione è la lettera formale di accettazione (*bukti diterima*) dell'istituto indonesiano ospitante [2].

---

### 2. GERARCHIA DELLE FONTI DI RIFERIMENTO (REGULATORY HIERARCHY)

#### A. Fonti Regolamentative Primarie (Livello Nazionale)
*   **Legge Nazionale (Tier 0)**: *Undang-Undang Nomor 6 Tahun 2011 tentang Keimigrasian* [6], come modificata dalla *Undang-Undang Nomor 63 Tahun 2024* [7].
*   **Regolamento Governativo**: *Peraturan Pemerintah (PP) Nomor 31 Tahun 2013* [8] e *Peraturan Pemerintah (PP) Nomor 45 Tahun 2024 tentang Jenis dan Tarif atas Jenis Penerimaan Negara Bukan Pajak (PNBP)* [9].
*   **Decreti Ministeriali (Kemenkumham / Kemenimipas)**: 
    *   *Peraturan Menteri Hukum dan HAM (Permenkumham) No. 22 del 2023* (in vigore dal 24 agosto 2023) [10, 11], modificata dal *Permenkumham No. 11 del 2024* (in vigore dal 3 maggio 2024) [12, 13].
    *   *Keputusan Menteri Imigrasi dan Pemasyarakatan (Kepmen M.IP-08.GR.01.01/2025)* sulla Classificazione dei Visti (in vigore dal 1° giugno 2025) [14].

#### B. Fonti Operative Ufficiali
*   Piattaforma digitale ufficiale della Direzione Generale dell'Immigrazione (*Direktorat Jenderal Imigrasi*): portali online `evisa.imigrasi.go.id` e `molina.imigrasi.go.id` [15, 16].

#### C. Interpretazioni Interne e Guide Esperte
*   Report di analisi e guide operative prodotte da *Bali Zero / Zantara Intelligence* (es. "Database dei visti Nuzantara 2025/2026" [17], "Guida alle procedure visti Bali Zero 2025" [18]).

---

### 3. ANALISI NORMATIVA DI DETTAGLIO: LEGITTIMITÀ, OPERATIVITÀ E VERIFICA DOCUMENTALE

Il diritto immigratorio indonesiano suddivide il soggiorno degli studenti stranieri in due percorsi principali: il soggiorno limitato (KITAS E30) e il soggiorno per visita a breve termine (C9).

#### A. Visto di Soggiorno Limitato per Studio (Student KITAS - Indice E30)
*   **Legittimamente Consentito**: Consente di risiedere in Indonesia per motivi di studio formale presso scuole o università registrate [5]. Copre l'istruzione primaria e secondaria (E30A) [19], l'istruzione superiore (diploma, laurea, master, dottorato - E30B) [20] e gli scambi studenteschi (E30F) [21]. **È vietato svolgere attività lavorativa**, ad eccezione di lavori part-time subordinati all'ottenimento di un'autorizzazione aggiuntiva speciale [5]. Consente di portare i membri della famiglia al seguito [3] e include automaticamente il permesso di rientro multiplo (MERP) per l'intera durata di validità della carta, eliminando la necessità di procedure separate ai sensi della riforma *UU No. 63 del 2024* [7].
*   **Operativamente Disponibile**: La domanda deve essere presentata online dal garante (*penjamin*) tramite l'applicazione ministeriale [1]. Il soggiorno limitato (ITB/KITAS) viene concesso per periodi massimi iniziali di **1 anno, 2 anni o 4 anni**, a seconda del programma di studio [4]. Il rinnovo annuale è di competenza del Capo dell'Ufficio Immigrazione locale (*Kepala Kantor Imigrasi*) territorialmente competente per il domicilio dello studente [22].
*   **Verifica Documentale**: Ai sensi del *Pasal 42 Permenkumham No. 22 del 2023*, il richiedente deve caricare [1, 2]:
    1. Passaporto ordinario valido per almeno 6 mesi [1].
    2. Garanzia finanziaria del garante (*bukti penjaminan*), che deve essere l'istituto di istruzione registrato o un cittadino indonesiano (WNI) [1].
    3. Prova del possesso di mezzi di sussistenza sufficienti (*costi di vita*) [2].
    4. Foto tessera a colori recente [2].
    5. Lettera formale di accettazione (*bukti diterima*) rilasciata dall'istituto di istruzione indonesiano, con l'indicazione esatta della durata del corso di studi (richiesta come "altro documento" obbligatorio ai sensi del Pasal 42 ayat (2)) [2].

#### B. Visto di Visita per Corsi Brevi (Short Study - Indice C9 / C9A / C9B)
*   **Legittimamente Consentito**: Consente soggiorni di studio non accademici, corsi brevi (es. lingua indonesiana - C9B [23], corsi keagamaan/religiosi - C9A [24], corsi di surf, yoga o cucina - C9 [25]). È tassativamente vietato lavorare [24].
*   **Operativamente Disponibile**: Visto a ingresso singolo (*single entry*) con durata iniziale di 60 giorni, prorogabile presso l'Ufficio Immigrazione fino a un massimo di **180 giorni totali** [25, 26].
*   **Verifica Documentale**: Richiede, oltre al passaporto (validità residua min. 6 mesi) e alla prova dei fondi di sussistenza, la **prova di registrazione o dichiarazione come partecipante** rilasciata da un ente governativo o da un istituto privato autorizzato [27].

#### C. Agevolazioni Nazionali per Borse di Studio (PNBP)
*   Ai sensi del *PP No. 45 del 2024, Pasal 5 ayat (4) lettera c*, gli studenti stranieri che beneficiano di una borsa di studio erogata dal Governo indonesiano sono esentati dal pagamento della tariffa del visto, applicando una tariffa governativa pari a **Rp 0,00 (esenzione totale)** [28].

---

### 4. FATTI DECISIVI, CONFLITTI, ALTERNATIVE E DOMANDE APERTE (GAPS)

#### I Fatti Decisivi
*   **Nessuna traccia di "Izin Belajar" ministeriale nelle leggi d'immigrazione**: L'analisi letterale del *Permenkumham No. 22 del 2023* e del *Permenkumham No. 11 del 2024* rivela che l'Immigrazione indonesiana approva il visto E30 unicamente sulla base della lettera di accettazione (*letter of acceptance*) della scuola, senza richiedere un'autorizzazione allo studio preventiva rilasciata da altri ministeri nel set di documenti standard codificato [1, 2].

#### Informazioni Mancanti e Gaps nelle Fonti (Incertezze)
*   **La proceduta dell'Izin Belajar esterno è omessa**: Poiché l'Izin Belajar è un documento regolato dal Ministero dell'Istruzione (*Kemendikbudristek*), la sua procedura di rilascio, i requisiti per le scuole e i tempi operativi non fanno parte del database immigratorio di NB-2. Per avere certezze assolute su questo passaggio preliminare, sarebbe necessario integrare nel notebook i regolamenti ministeriali del *Kemendikbudristek* o del *Kemenag* (per gli istituti religiosi).

#### Alternative d'Azione per lo Studente
*   Se l'istituto ospitante non è accreditato per sponsorizzare un KITAS E30, l'unica alternativa legale disponibile nelle fonti per svolgere studi a breve termine (non accademici) è l'ottenimento del visto di visita **C9** (60-180 giorni) [25].

#### Conflitti Normativi e Amministrativi
*   **Transizione Istituzionale (Kemenimipas)**: Dalla fine del 2024, le competenze immigratorie sono passate dal vecchio *Kemenkumham* al nuovo ministero dedicato *Kemenimipas* (Ministero dell'Immigrazione e degli Affari Penitenziari) [29, 30]. La mancanza di decreti attuativi dettagliati (*Petunjuk Teknis / Juknis*) di questo nuovo ministero genera incertezze operative sulla standardizzazione delle piattaforme digitali e sulla potenziale richiesta di raccomandazioni interministeriali per i visti E30.

#### Regole Locali Bali vs. Regole Nazionali
*   La regolamentazione scolastica e la disciplina keimigrasian dei permessi di soggiorno per motivi di studio sono di competenza **esclusivamente nazionale** (gestite dal Kemenimipas e dalla Ditjen Imigrasi a Jakarta) [30].
*   Non esistono leggi regionali di Bali (*Perda*) che disciplinano l'istruzione degli stranieri. Tuttavia, a livello operativo locale a Bali, la task force **"Dharma Dewata"** (attiva da aprile 2026) esegue pattugliamenti e controlli serrati nelle zone calde (Canggu, Ubud, Uluwatu) [31, 32]. Qualsiasi studente con KITAS E30 o visto C9 che venga sorpreso a svolgere attività commerciali, promozioni sponsorizzate o lavoro locale (anche non retribuito/baratto) viene immediatamente deportato per violazione delle condizioni del soggiorno ai sensi del *Pasal 122 della UU No. 6 del 2011* [33, 34].

---

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Section 4 — PLAIN-LANGUAGE DEFINITION (5 bullets, citable) What the C5A "Visa Kunjungan Konten Kreator" BANS and PERMITS — for an Indonesian content-creator beneficiary: PERMITTED — creating content. A C5A holder may shoot, film and produce social-media content in Indonesia. That creative act is the visa's purpose ("Visa Kunjungan Konten Kreator"). (Basis: the visa category itself, Kepmen M.IP-08.GR.01.01/2025; sibling C5 "Dengan visa ini, anda dapat ... peliputan".) PERMITTED — being paid by a FOREIGN source. Income from outside Indonesia — a foreign brand, a foreign agency, Google AdSense (Google Ireland/US), a foreign employer — does not trigger the prohibition, because the ban is specifically on reward "dari perorangan atau korporasi DI INDONESIA." (The E33G row confirms the same logic: it requires "perjanjian kerja dengan perusahaan yang didirikan di luar Wilayah Indonesia.") BANNED — selling goods or services locally. Selling any product or service while on this visa is prohibited: "dilarang menjual barang atau jasa." (Basis: C5 , live; same family for C5A.) BANNED — any reward from an Indonesian person or company, INCLUDING in-kind/barter. Receiving "imbalan, upah, atau sejenisnya ... dari perorangan atau korporasi di Indonesia" is prohibited. "Imbalan ... atau sejenisnya" (reward ... or the like) covers non-monetary compensation — a free villa/hotel stay, a sponsored experience, services in kind — because Indonesian labour law itself counts "imbalan dalam bentuk lain" (reward in another form) as compensation (UU 13/2003 Pasal 1 angka 3-4). No money has to change hands for it to be banned. WHY — it's the SOURCE and the BENEFICIARY, not the cash. Indonesian immigration judges the substance of the activity: purpose of arrival, form of activity, and economic impact — and criminalises activity inconsistent with the permit (UU 6/2011 Pasal 122), with the enabling Indonesian party exposed to the same penalty (Pasal 122 letter b). Work that benefits an Indonesian business and is rewarded by that Indonesian business is, in substance, local employment requiring a work permit/RPTKA (PP 34/2021) — barter does not escape this.

question:
May a visitor attend short courses, workshops or language school on C1/B1? Where is the line versus formal E30 study?

Use only the sources already in NB-2. Answer with concrete conclusions, do not default to requesting human review. Separate primary regulatory sources, official operational sources, and internal interpretations. For every claim give source title, date, passage and source ID. Distinguish what is legally permitted, what is operationally available, and what requires document verification. List the decisive facts, missing questions, alternatives and conflicts. If the sources do not allow a conclusion, state exactly which information or source is missing.
answer:
### 1. Executive Summary

Under the current Indonesian Keimigrasian legal framework, a sharp legal distinction exists between casual recreational activities and structured, non-degree, or formal academic study. 

*   **Casual or Drop-in Activities (C1 / B1)**: Visitors holding a **C1 Tourism Visit Visa** or **B1 Visa on Arrival (VOA)** are legally permitted to participate only in unstructured, highly informal, or one-off activities under the scope of "personal development" (*pengembangan pribadi*) [1, 2]. This includes drop-in sessions (e.g., a single yoga class, a one-day Balinese cooking workshop, or a casual surfing lesson) [1, 3].
*   **Structured Short Courses & Language Schools (C9 / C9B)**: Enrolling in structured, multi-week, or curriculum-based courses (such as a registered language school, a yoga teacher training course, or an organized surf school program) is **strictly prohibited on a C1 or B1 visa** [4, 5]. Foreigners participating in these programs must hold a **C9 Short Study Visit Visa** (or **C9B** specifically for Bahasa Indonesia) sponsored by a registered training institution (*lembaga pendidikan/kursus*) [3, 6].
*   **Formal Degree/Academic Study (E30)**: Formal, degree-granting academic studies or long-term school enrollments are strictly reserved for the **E30 Student ITAS/KITAS** (and its sub-indices), sponsored exclusively by accredited Indonesian schools or universities [7].

Violating these stay permit boundaries constitutes a major immigration offense under national law (**UU No. 6/2011 Pasal 122**), which exposes both the foreign student and the local sponsoring business to severe administrative and criminal penalties [4, 8]. In Bali, local enforcement is heavily active through **Tim PORA Kuta Selatan** [9] and the **Dharma Dewata Patrol Task Force** [10, 11], which actively target unauthorized activities in tourist hubs like Canggu, Seminyak, and Ubud [4, 9].

---

### 2. Primary Regulatory Sources (National Level)

The national legal framework is governed by the primary laws, government regulations, and ministerial decrees of the Republic of Indonesia.

#### A. Visa C1 (Tourism Single-Entry)
*   **Legal Status**: Legally defined as a single-entry visitor stay permit (*Izin Tinggal Kunjungan* - ITK) [12].
*   **Legally Permitted Activities**: Under **Kepmen M.IP-08.GR.01.01/2025 Lampiran A (effective June 1, 2025)**, the C1 visa permits:
    > *"Mengunjungi tempat tertentu untuk tujuan rekreasi, pengembangan pribadi, atau mempelajari keunikan daya tarik wisata..."* (Visiting specific places for recreation, personal development, or studying the unique attractions of tourism...) [1, 2].
*   **Stay Duration**: Initially granted for **60 days**, extendable up to a maximum cumulative stay of **180 days** per year [2, 13, 14].
*   **Source Citation**: *Kepmen M.IP-08.GR.01.01/2025 — Klasifikasi Visa (110-tipe, include C5A)*, May 2, 2025, Passage Index 10/454.

#### B. Visa B1 (Tourism Visa on Arrival - VOA)
*   **Legal Status**: Legally defined as a short-term visitor stay permit obtained at the border (TPI) [12, 15].
*   **Legally Permitted Activities**: Restricted strictly to tourism, family visits, transit, and MICE (meetings, incentives, conventions, and exhibitions) attendance as a participant [16, 17].
*   **Stay Duration**: **30 days**, extendable once for an additional **30 days** (maximum 60 days total); **strictly non-convertible** to any long-term stay permit (ITAS) in-country [16, 18].
*   **Source Citation**: *visto_voa_b1b2b3b4_guida_2025.txt*, March 2025 / *nb2_visa_types_final.txt*, March 2026, Passage Index 393/682/711.

#### C. Visa C9 / C9A / C9B (Short Study & Training)
*   **Legal Status**: Single-entry visitor visa designed specifically for non-formal, non-degree educational courses and short training programs [6].
*   **Legally Permitted Activities**:
    *   **C9**: Comparative study (*studi banding*), short courses (*kursus singkat*), and short training (*pelatihan singkat*) [6, 19].
    *   **C9A**: Non-degree religious short-term training [20, 21].
    *   **C9B**: Non-degree Indonesian language courses (*Bahasa Indonesia*) [22, 23].
*   **Stay Duration**: **60 days**, extendable up to a maximum of **180 days** [3, 6].
*   **Source Citation**: *Kepmen M.IP-08.GR.01.01/2025 — Klasifikasi Visa*, May 2, 2025, Passage Index 23/24/25.

#### D. Visa E30 / E30A / E30B / E30E / E30F (Student ITAS)
*   **Legal Status**: Limited Stay Permit (*Izin Tinggal Terbatas* - ITB / KITAS) issued for formal educational enrollment [7, 24, 25].
*   **Legally Permitted Activities**:
    *   **E30**: General formal education in Indonesia [7, 24].
    *   **E30A**: Primary and secondary education [26].
    *   **E30B**: Higher education (diploma, bachelor, master, doctorate programs) [27].
    *   **E30E**: Formal studies at an educational institution in a Special Economic Zone (KEK) [28].
    *   **E30F**: Formal academic student exchange programs [29].
*   **Stay Duration**: **1 year, 2 years, or up to 4 years** depending on the academic cycle, renewable in-country [7, 30, 31].
*   **Source Citation**: *Kepmen M.IP-08.GR.01.01/2025 — Klasifikasi Visa*, May 2, 2025, Passage Index 58/60/62/64/65.

---

### 3. Official Operational Sources

Operational processes and document requirements are managed digitally via the e-Visa portal and local offices.

#### A. Document Verification Requirements
*   **For C1 / B1 (Tourism/VOA)**:
    *   Passport with a minimum validity of **6 months** [2, 16].
    *   Proof of sufficient living expenses (minimum **USD 2,000** for C1; minimum **USD 1,000** or equivalent for B1) [2, 16].
    *   Return or onward travel ticket [2, 16].
    *   *Source Citation*: *nb2_visa_types_final.txt*, March 2026, Passage Index 361/393/654/682.
*   **For C9 / C9B (Short Study/Language School)**:
    *   Passport with a minimum validity of **6 months** [32].
    *   Under **Permenkumham No. 11 Tahun 2024 Pasal 16 Ayat 5 Huruf h**, applicants must provide a formal **letter of acceptance or proof of registration as a participant** (*tanda bukti terdaftar atau keterangan sebagai peserta*) from a registered private training provider or government agency in Indonesia [33, 34].
    *   Proof of funds (*bukti memiliki biaya hidup*) [32].
    *   *Source Citation*: *https://peraturan.go.id/files/permenkumham-no-11-tahun-2024.pdf*, May 3, 2024, Passage Index 189/561.
*   **For E30 (Student ITAS)**:
    *   Passport with a minimum validity of **6 months** [35].
    *   Under **Permenkumham No. 22 Tahun 2023 Pasal 42 Ayat (1) & (2)**, requires a **formal guarantee letter (*bukti penjaminan*)** from an accredited Indonesian educational institution and a formal admission certificate detailing the duration of the degree program [35-38].
    *   Proof of sufficient living expenses [35, 36].
    *   *Source Citation*: *Permenkumham_22_2023.pdf*, August 22, 2023, Passage Index 143/144/204/205.

#### B. Portal Availability
*   Applications for C1, B1 (e-VOA), C9, and E30 are processed digitally through the Directorate General of Immigration's portal (**molina.imigrasi.go.id / evisa.imigrasi.go.id**) [39, 40].
*   C9 and C9B visas are operationally available but require the sponsoring course provider to be registered in the e-Visa database to issue the invitation/acceptance letters required for system approval [3, 33].

---

### 4. Internal Interpretations & Expert Guides

According to the internal intelligence platform and client database of **Bali Zero (Zantara Intelligence)**, several operational realities shape the gray areas:

*   **Drop-In vs. Organized Enrollment**: Highly informal, one-off lessons (such as a single yoga class or a half-day cooking workshop) do not involve formal enrollment or institutional registration. These are operationally treated as recreational "personal development" and are tolerated under C1 or B1 tourist visas [1, 3].
*   **The School Enrollment Trap**: If a foreigner enrolls in a structured multi-week or multi-month language program, yoga teacher training, or surf academy while holding only a C1/B1 visa, this is an immediate **red flag** [4]. In the event of a field audit (*Sidak*), the school must show a C9 (Short Study) sponsorship for that student; failing to do so exposes both parties to prosecution [4, 8].
*   **Source of Funds**: Because C9 and C9B visas strictly prohibit earning local income [22, 41], students are allowed to receive only passive financial support from abroad, or a minor stipend/reimbursement of expenses in specific training/internship formats [42].
*   *Source Citation*: *nb2_visa_procedures_guide.txt*, March 2026 / *visto_c12_c18_c22_guida_2025.txt*, March 27, 2025, Passage Index 410/608.

---

### 5. The Decisive Hinge: Drawing the Line Versus E30 Study

| Feature / Criteria | **Short Study (C9 / C9B)** | **Formal Study (E30 / E30B)** |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Primary Hinge (The Line)** | Non-degree courses, non-academic short training, or language schools [6]. | Accredited academic degree programs (diploma, bachelor, master, doctorate) or formal schools [7, 27]. |
| **Visa Category** | Visit Visa (*Visa Kunjungan*) [43, 44]. | Limited Stay Permit (*Izin Tinggal Terbatas* / ITAS / KITAS) [7]. |
| **Maximum Duration** | Initial 60 days, extendable up to a maximum of **180 days** [3, 6]. | **1, 2, or up to 4 years** depending on the academic cycle, renewable in-country [7, 30, 31]. |
| **Guarantor / Sponsor** | Registered private training center, language school, or course provider (*lembaga pendidikan/kursus*) [3, 6]. | Accredited primary/secondary school or higher education university [7]. |
| **In-Country Transition** | Convertible to an ITAS (e.g., E30 or E28) via an *Alih Status* process if sponsored [2, 6]. | Can lead directly to a Permanent Stay Permit (*Izin Tinggal Tetap* / KITAP) after 3 years [45]. |

*   *Source Citations*: *nb2_visa_types_final.txt*, March 2026 / *visto_c12_c18_c22_guida_2025.txt*, March 27, 2025, Passage Index 323/390/624/679.

---

### 6. National Rules vs. Bali Local Regulations & Enforcement

While national laws set visa classifications, regional offices in Bali enforce them with a zero-tolerance policy.

*   **Tim PORA & Dharma Dewata Patrols**: Under **UU No. 6/2011 Pasal 122**, executing activities inconsistent with the purpose of a stay permit is a criminal offense [8]. 
    *   **Pasal 122(a)** penalizes the foreigner with up to **5 years imprisonment** and a fine of up to **Rp 500,000,000**, followed by deportation and blacklisting [8, 46].
    *   **Pasal 122(b)** penalizes the sponsoring or enabling local party (such as a language school or yoga center that enrolls tourists on C1/B1) with the **same** penalty [8].
*   **Enforcement Focus**: The **Dharma Dewata Patrol Task Force (launched April 2026)** and **Tim PORA Kuta Selatan** conduct unannounced inspections (*Sidak*) and actively monitor social media in Canggu, Seminyak, and Ubud [4, 9, 10]. They specifically cross-verify student registries at local centers to check if attendees hold the mandatory C9/C9B visas [4].
*   **Tourist Levy**: In addition to immigration compliance, all foreign visitors entering Bali must pay the **Rp 150,000 Bali Tourist Levy** under **Perda Bali No. 2/2025 (superseding Perda No. 6/2023)** via lovebali.baliprov.go.id, regardless of whether they hold a C1 or B1 visa [47-49].
*   *Source Citations*: *2026-06-01-c5a-local-ban-sources.md*, June 1, 2026 / *T4 Source — Kantor Imigrasi Ngurah Rai Official Channels + Tim Pora Intel*, March 2026, Passage Index 857/860/1021/1022.

---

### 7. Gaps, Conflicts, and Missing Information

An adversarial analysis of the legal framework reveals several structural conflicts and missing regulatory components:

1.  **Multiple-Entry Visa Exclusion (The C9 Gap)**:
    *   *The Conflict*: Under **Permenkumham No. 11/2024 Pasal 15 Ayat (1)**, multiple-entry visitor visas (D-indices) list tourism, business, and MICE as permitted activities, but **studi banding, kursus singkat, and pelatihan singkat (C9) are completely excluded** [50, 51].
    *   *The Consequence*: Frequent short-term students or trainees cannot use multiple-entry visas to attend recurring classes. They must apply for a new Single-Entry C9 visa every time or exploit the tourist "personal development" gray area, creating high administrative friction [3, 51].
2.  **Ambiguity of "Personal Development" (*Pengembangan Pribadi*)**:
    *   *The Gap*: There is no formal definition or official implementing guide (*Petunjuk Teknis - Juknis*) from the newly restructured **Kemenimipas (formed in late 2024)** [52, 53] that sets a clear threshold for where "personal development" under C1 ends and "short course study" under C9 begins (e.g., number of hours, days, or course structure).
    *   *The Risk*: This allows individual immigration officers at local offices (Kanim Ngurah Rai or Denpasar) to exercise arbitrary discretion during Tim PORA audits, increasing the risk of unexpected detentions or fines [4].
3.  **Accreditation Verification for Course Sponsoring**:
    *   *The Missing Information*: The regulations fail to specify the exact licensing requirements (such as Dinas Pendidikan or Kemendikbud accreditation) a private Balinese business (like a surf school or yoga studio) must possess to legally sponsor a C9/C9B visa.

question:
For E33G, define precisely: employer abroad, no Indonesian clients, no Indonesian-source income — which of these are explicit legal conditions vs operational practice? May an E33G holder's foreign employer have Indonesian customers if the holder does not serve them?

Use only the sources already in NB-2. Answer with concrete conclusions, do not default to requesting human review. Separate primary regulatory sources, official operational sources, and internal interpretations. For every claim give source title, date, passage and source ID. Distinguish what is legally permitted, what is operationally available, and what requires document verification. List the decisive facts, missing questions, alternatives and conflicts. If the sources do not allow a conclusion, state exactly which information or source is missing.
answer:
### I. DIRECT DEFINITIONS: LEGAL CONDITIONS VS. OPERATIONAL PRACTICES

The remote worker framework under the **E33G stay permit index** is governed by strict national statutory boundaries, but it also relies heavily on practical verification tolerances. 

*   **Employer Abroad**: This is an **explicit legal condition** defined under national regulations. 
    *   *Primary Regulatory Source*: **Permenkumham No. 22/2023** (as amended by **Permenkumham No. 11/2024**), **Pasal 33 ayat (2) huruf j angka 5** and **Pasal 63 ayat (1)** `[1, 2]`.
    *   *Date*: Enacted August 22, 2023 (No. 22/2023) and April 1, 2024 (No. 11/2024).
    *   *Specific Passage*: The law defines the holder as a "remote worker who has an employment relationship with a company outside Indonesian territory" (*pekerja jarak jauh yang terikat hubungan kerja dengan perusahaan di luar Wilayah Indonesia*) `[1]`, specifically a "company not domiciled in Indonesia" (*perusahaan yang tidak berkedudukan di Indonesia*) `[2]`. 
    *   *Source ID / Document*: `Permenkumham_22_2023.pdf` & `Permenkumham_11_2024.pdf`.
*   **No Indonesian Clients**: This is an **explicit legal condition** for the **individual visa holder** (prohibiting them from local sales and labor), but it is an **operational practice** when interpreted as a restriction on the employer's client base.
    *   *Primary Regulatory Source / Official Operational Portal*: Verbatim **E33G "Ketentuan lain" (prohibition list)** from the Directorate General of Immigration portal `[3]`.
    *   *Date*: June 1, 2026 (Portal fetch date).
    *   *Specific Passage*: "You are prohibited from staying in Indonesian territory beyond the stay-permit period, from doing work that does not conform to the stay permit, from selling goods or services, except where required in [the performance of] their [remote] work" `[3]`.
    *   *Source ID / Document*: `2026-06-01-c5a-local-ban-sources.md`.
    *   *Expert Guide Interpretation*: *KITAS E33G Remote Work Guida 2025* `[4]`.
    *   *Specific Passage*: "Il richiedente NON deve lavorare per aziende indonesiane... Questa è la distinzione legale cruciale rispetto al KITAS E23." `[4]`.
*   **No Indonesian-Source Income**: This is an **explicit legal condition** verified during both application and territory-wide enforcement.
    *   *Primary Regulatory Source / Official Operational Portal*: **E33G "Persyaratan khusus" (special requirements)** from the Directorate General of Immigration `[5]`.
    *   *Date*: June 1, 2026 (Portal fetch date).
    *   *Specific Passage*: Requires an "Employment agreement with a company established outside Indonesian territory" (*Perjanjian kerja dengan perusahaan yang didirikan di luar Wilayah Indonesia*) alongside proof of "income... of at least US\$60,000 per year" `[5]`. 
    *   *Source ID / Document*: `2026-06-01-c5a-local-ban-sources.md`.
    *   *Expert Guide Interpretation*: *Garante / Penjamin Guida 2025* `[6]`.
    *   *Specific Passage*: "E' vietato lavorare per aziende indonesiane o generare reddito locale [IMM-364]." `[6]`.
    *   *Source ID / Document*: `garante_penjamin_guida_2025.txt`.

#### May an E33G holder's foreign employer have Indonesian customers if the holder does not serve them?
**Yes. This is legally permitted.** 
*   **Legal Reasoning**: Indonesian immigration jurisdiction operates on an individual, activity-centric territorial basis. **Pasal 1 angka 26 of UU No. 6 Tahun 2011** binds stay permits to the foreigner's specific *kegiatan* (activity) `[7]`. The E33G legal definition restricts the **individual worker** from engaging in local commercial sales or providing local services (*"melakukan penjualan barang atau jasa"* ) `[3]`. It requires that the foreign employer be established outside Indonesian territory (*"perusahaan di luar Wilayah Indonesia"* ) `[5]`. 
*   Because the corporate employer is a separate legal entity not domiciled in Indonesia, **the employer is legally permitted to have Indonesian B2B or B2C customers**, provided that the E33G holder has **absolute zero involvement** in serving, managing, or transacting with those Indonesian customers. Any direct involvement by the E33G holder would immediately cross the line into unauthorized local work, triggering the penalties of **Pasal 122 of UU No. 6 Tahun 2011** `[8]`.

---

### II. CLASSIFICATION OF SOURCES

#### A. Primary Regulatory Sources (National Level)
1.  **UU No. 6 Tahun 2011 tentang Keimigrasian** (as amended by **UU No. 63/2024**): National primary law framing the legal boundaries of stay permits based on the foreigner's activities (*kegiatan*) and penalties for permit misuse under Pasal 122 `[7-9]`.
2.  **PP No. 40/2023 & PP No. 63/2023**: Government Regulations establishing the "Second Home" stay permit subclass, which officially introduced the E33G Remote Worker KITAS into the national system `[10]`.
3.  **Permenkumham No. 22/2023 (as amended by Permenkumham No. 11/2024)**: Ministerial regulations detailing the remote work visa requirements under Pasal 33 and the application procedures under Pasal 63 `[1, 2, 11]`.

#### B. Official Operational Sources
1.  **Directorate General of Immigration Index Portal (`imigrasi.go.id/wna/daftar-visa-indonesia/E33G`)**: The official, live, public-facing database detailing standard special requirements and prohibitions for remote workers `[3, 5, 8]`.
2.  **e-Visa Application Platform (`evisa.imigrasi.go.id`)**: The national digital submission portal where remote workers upload their verified foreign employment contracts `[12]`.

#### C. Internal Interpretations and Expert Guides (Bali Zero / Zantara Intelligence)
1.  **KITAS E33G Remote Work Guide 2025** (`kitas_e33g_remote_work_guida_2025.txt`): Analyzes in-country processing, local office application, and tax exposures in Bali `[4, 10, 12-18]`.
2.  **C5A Local-Work Prohibition Analysis** (`2026-06-01-c5a-local-ban-sources.md`): Compares the definitions of "imbalan" (in-kind reward) under labor law (*UU No. 13/2003*) and immigration prohibitions across content creators and remote workers `[3, 5, 7-9, 19-32]`.
3.  **Guida al Sistema del Garante 2025** (`garante_penjamin_guida_2025.txt`): Examines self-sponsorship via immigration/financial guarantee for E33G in place of local corporate sponsors `[6, 33-38]`.
4.  **Bali Zero Client FAQ Database** (`nb2_faq_clienti.txt`): Practical advisory database detailing real-world client-case outcomes, digital nomad practices, and tax residency triggers `[39-42]`.

---

### III. LEGAL, OPERATIONAL, AND DOCUMENT VERIFICATION MATRIX

| Legally Permitted (National Law) | Operationally Available (Molina/Local Imigrasi) | Requires Document Verification (Gateway) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Perform Online Work**: Exclusively for foreign employers or foreign clients `[14]`. | **Self-Sponsorship**: Bypasses local Indonesian corporate guarantors using a financial guarantee instead `[15]`. | **Foreign Contract**: A valid employment agreement or foreign client-contract clearly established with a company outside Indonesia `[4, 5]`. |
| **Use Coworking Spaces**: Lawfully utilize shared office infrastructures across Bali (Canggu, Ubud) `[14]`. | **Dependent Sponsorship**: Sponsor spouses/children for family reunification stay permits (**Index E31D**) `[39]`. | **The Income Gate**: Verifiable proof of foreign-sourced income of at least **USD 60,000 per year** `[4, 5]`. |
| **Open Personal Bank Accounts**: Open local savings accounts (e.g., BCA, Mandiri) in Indonesia `[14]`. | **Multiple Entry (MERP)**: Freely travel in and out of the country; the MERP is integrated directly into the E33G KITAS card `[43]`. | **Bank Statements**: Bank statements showing at least USD 2,000 for the last 3 months to demonstrate immediate liquid solvency `[4]`. |
| **Sign Residential Leases**: Legally rent long-term villas or houses in Indonesia `[14]`. | **Alih Status (In-Country)**: Change status in-country from a tourist/visit visa (**C1/C18**) directly to E33G, avoiding offshore exit `[44, 45]`. | **Passport Validity**: Minimum of **6 months** residua legally required `[46]`, although **18 months** is highly recommended operationally `[4]`. |
| **Path to Permanent Stay (KITAP)**: Transition to a Permanent Stay Permit after **3 consecutive years** of valid E33G KITAS `[18]`. | **No RPTKA Required**: Operationally faster and cheaper than standard work permits as no Ministry of Manpower approval is needed `[47]`. | **Health Insurance**: Valid health insurance coverage active within the territory of Indonesia `[4]`. |

---

### IV. DECISIVE FACTS, CONFLICTS, ALTERNATIVES, AND OMISSIONS

#### 1. Decisive Facts (The Hinge)
The absolute legal hinge that separates E33G from standard local work permits (E23 KITAS) is **the corporate domicile of the employer and the source of funds** `[10, 17]`. Under **PP No. 34 Tahun 2021**, any work performed for an Indonesian company or generating local Indonesian income requires a Ministry of Manpower approved **RPTKA** and prepaid **DKP-TKA levy** (USD 100/month) `[48, 49]`. E33G bypasses Manpower ministry oversight entirely because the work is structured solely within a foreign corporate relationship and paid from overseas `[10, 17]`.

#### 2. Alternatives
*   **C5A Visit Visa (Content Creator)**: If the foreigner’s stay is short-term (60–180 days) and they do not require stable residency `[41, 50]`. It permits generating creative content in Indonesia while receiving Google AdSense or foreign brand sponsorship from overseas `[31, 42]`.
*   **E28A Investor KITAS**: If the nomad actually wishes to incorporate a business, open local retail offices, or invest capital in Indonesia (minimum Rp 10 billion in shares) `[51-53]`.

#### 3. Conflicts and Regulatory Gaps
*   **The Income Threshold Mismatch**: There is a severe mismatch between **national primary regulations** (which dictate a strict proof of income of at least **USD 60,000 per year** `[4-6]`) and **local agency/FAQ guidelines** (which state that bank statements showing at least **USD 2,000 per month**—which equates to only USD 24,000/year—are sufficient to apply `[41, 45, 54]`). Applying under the lower USD 2,000/month guide represents a critical rejection risk if local immigration officers strictly enforce the national decree's USD 60,000/year requirement.
*   **The 183-Day Personal Tax Trap**: While operational guides market the E33G as allowing nomads to maintain their tax domicile in their home country `[54]`, **national Indonesian tax law** mandates that any foreigner residing in Indonesia for **183+ days within any 12-month period** automatically becomes an Indonesian tax resident `[16, 50]`. This legally subjects their global remote income to Indonesian personal income tax (PPh OP), turning E33G residency into a potential global tax trap.

#### 4. Missing Information / Open Questions
*   **Ministry Restructuring Petunjuk Teknis (Juknis)**: Since the ministry restructured from Kemenkumham to the newly formed **Kemenimipas** (Ministry of Immigration and Correctional Affairs) under the Prabowo cabinet in late 2024 `[55, 56]`, **there are no official Juknis documents in the current sources** outlining how the new ministry strictly audits the E33G's USD 60,000/year income threshold (e.g., whether they demand certified tax returns or simply accept basic bank statements).
*   **UU No. 1 Tahun 2026**: As flagged in the change monitoring digest (`OQ-003`), it is currently an open question whether the newly proposed **UU No. 1 Tahun 2026 tentang Imigrasi** will further modify, restrict, or replace the remote worker stay permit rules established under UU 63/2024 and Permenkumham 22/2023 `[57]`. The full gazette text is currently missing from the sources.

This brief documents ONE narrow point for a Bali Zero editorial piece: under the C5A "Visa Kunjungan Konten Kreator" , a foreign creator may CREATE social-media content but is prohibited from any value-exchange with an Indonesian beneficiary — including non-monetary compensation (barter: free villa/hotel stay, sponsored experience, services in kind) . The legal hinge is the phrase "imbalan, upah, atau sejenisnya" ("reward, wage, or the like ") in the visa-classification Larangan , reinforced by the Indonesian-immigration doctrine that what matters is (a) the SOURCE of the benefit and (b) the BENEFICIARY of the activity — not whether money changed hands.

" This single sentence is the doctrinal core. It contains TWO independent bans joined by "atau" (or): "menjual barang atau jasa" — selling goods or services (the local-commerce ban); and "menerima imbalan, upah, atau sejenisnya ... dari perorangan atau korporasi di Indonesia" — receiving reward, wage, or the like from an Indonesian person or company (the local-benefit ban).

The most precise read requires THREE definitions, not one: Pasal 1 angka 30 — Upah (verbatim ID): "Upah adalah hak pekerja/buruh yang diterima dan dinyatakan dalam bentuk uang sebagai imbalan dari pengusaha atau pemberi kerja kepada pekerja/buruh yang ditetapkan dan dibayarkan menurut suatu perjanjian kerja, kesepakatan, atau peraturan perundang-undangan, termasuk tunjangan bagi pekerja/buruh dan keluarganya atas suatu pekerjaan dan/atau jasa yang telah atau akan dilakukan."

"Pemberi kerja adalah orang perseorangan, pengusaha, badan hukum, atau badan-badan lainnya yang mempekerjakan tenaga kerja dengan membayar upah atau imbalan dalam bentuk lain ." EN: "An employer is a natural person, entrepreneur, legal entity, or other body that employs labour by paying a wage or reward in another form ." Analysis (this is the load-bearing nuance — handle precisely in the piece): The narrow term "upah" (angka 30) is, on its face, monetary ("dinyatakan dalam bentuk uang"). If the editorial relied ONLY on the labour-law definition of upah , a literalist could argue a free villa is "not upah" because no money moves. BUT the legal concepts that actually define WHO is a worker and WHO is an employer (angka 3 and angka 4) both explicitly include "imbalan dalam bentuk lain" — reward in another form , i.e. non-monetary / in-kind . Indonesian labour law itself therefore treats an in-kind reward as enough to constitute an employment relationship. This dovetails exactly with the immigration Larangan 's "imbalan, upah, atau sejenisnya" : the immigration text deliberately lists "imbalan" FIRST (the broad, not-necessarily-monetary term) and adds "atau sejenisnya" (or the like). It is not limited to "upah"/cash. A comped villa night given by an Indonesian villa in exchange for a Reel is an "imbalan ... dari ... korporasi di Indonesia" — squarely inside the ban.

Citable formulation for the piece: "Indonesian labour law defines a worker as anyone who works for a wage or reward in another form (UU 13/2003 Pasal 1 angka 3), and an employer as anyone who pays a wage or reward in another form (angka 4). The immigration prohibition mirrors this: it bans receiving imbalan, upah, atau sejenisnya — reward, wage, or the like . In-kind value (a free stay) is imbalan . No money needs to change hands." --------------------------------------------------------------------------------

3b. PP No. 34 Tahun 2021 tentang Penggunaan Tenaga Kerja Asing [VERIFIED — text-extracted via pdftotext from the provincial primary copy (llg-bwi.org); abstract cross-checked on peraturan.bpk.go.id/Details/161898] Pasal 1 angka 1 — TKA (verbatim ID) — "work" is defined by intent, not by payment form: "Tenaga Kerja Asing yang selanjutnya disingkat TKA adalah warga negara asing pemegang visa dengan maksud bekerja di wilayah Indonesia." Pasal 1 angka 2 — Pemberi Kerja TKA (verbatim ID) — the in-kind hinge again:

Pasal 4 ayat (1) (verbatim ID) — work must be inside a formal employment relationship: "TKA hanya dapat dipekerjakan oleh Pemberi Kerja TKA dalam hubungan kerja untuk jabatan tertentu dan waktu tertentu, serta memiliki kompetensi sesuai dengan jabatan yang akan diduduki." Synthesis of 3a + 3b — the doctrine, stated for the piece: Immigration ties lawful stay to kegiatan (the permitted activity ) and to a responsible Penjamin/beneficiary (UU 6/2011 Pasal 1 angka 26), and criminalises activity that does not match the permit (Pasal 122) — payment is never an element of the offence. The labour framework defines an "employer of a TKA" as anyone who provides a wage OR reward in another form (PP 34/2021 Pasal 1 angka 2; UU 13/2003 Pasal 1 angka 4). Therefore: a foreigner who performs promotional work for the benefit of an Indonesian business and receives an in-kind reward from that Indonesian business has (i) performed kegiatan inconsistent with a content-creator visit visa, and (ii) entered a relationship that, in substance, is employment by an Indonesian beneficiary requiring a work permit/RPTKA — regardless of whether cash moved. What disqualifies it is the Indonesian source/beneficiary , not the form of pay.

3c.
